title: Threads and Ownership
goal: Spawn OS threads, move owned data into thread closures, and join threads to get results.

sections.text: In Go or C++, threads can easily capture local variables from outer scopes. Rust threads created with `thread::spawn` run independently and might outlive the stack frame that created them.

sections.caption: `thread::spawn` runs a closure on a new thread and returns a `JoinHandle`.

sections.text: Because a thread can run for any length of time, captured data must live for `'static` or be moved in. Passing borrowed references triggers compiler error `E0373`.

sections.caption: The `move` keyword transfers ownership of `msg` into the closure.

sections.text: Calling `join()` on a `JoinHandle` blocks until that thread completes. It returns a `Result` containing the closure return value or panic payload.

sections.code:
let handle = thread::spawn(|| 42);
let result: i32 = handle.join().unwrap();
sections.caption: Joining a thread retrieves the return value from its closure.

sections.text: Sharing mutable state safely across multiple threads requires atomic reference counting and mutexes, which are covered in the next deck.

explanation: Spawn OS threads, move owned data into thread closures, and join threads to get results.
